headline: Spain's Ávila Wildfire Becomes Largest in Spanish History at 111,000 Acres as Dual Heat Domes Bake Europe and the US Southwest with 120°F Extremes
overview: A catastrophic wildfire in Spain's Ávila province has surpassed 111,000 acres — consuming an area five times the size of Barcelona — and is now officially the largest wildfire in Spanish recorded history, as it remains only partially stabilized. Simultaneously, two concurrent heat domes continue to intensify: the US Southwest is enduring life-threatening temperatures of 115–120°F through Sunday across Arizona, California's Coachella Valley, and the Mojave Desert, while Europe's heat dome drives Berlin to 37.5°C with 40°C+ conditions forecast to persist well into August. Separate wildfire and seismic emergencies in Oregon and the Texas Panhandle add to a globally active natural hazard landscape.

events.title: Spain–France Wildfires: Ávila Fire Becomes Largest in Spanish History at 111,000 Acres
events.location: Ávila Province, Castilla y León, Spain; Gironde, France
events.summary: The wildfire burning in Ávila province has now scorched 111,000 acres (193 square miles — five times the area of Barcelona), confirmed by officials as the largest wildfire in Spanish recorded history. French authorities described the Gironde blaze as 'stabilized but not contained,' while Spanish firefighters on the ground stated the fire was effectively uncontrollable under prevailing conditions. More than 200,000 people remain displaced across Castilla y León, Madrid, Ávila, Guadalajara, and the French Gironde, with extreme wildfire danger expected to persist through the ongoing European heat dome.

events.title: US Heat Dome Reaches Peak Intensity — 115–120°F in Arizona and Coachella Valley Through Sunday
events.location: Arizona, California, Nevada, Utah, Montana, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, USA
events.summary: The US heat dome has reached its most dangerous phase, with NWS Extreme Heat Warnings now active across more than 20 distinct zones spanning Arizona through Montana and including Puerto Rico. The Coachella Valley, Yuma, and Parker Valley in Arizona and California face forecast highs of 115–120°F through Sunday, August 2, with Phoenix's metropolitan area under a Major-to-Extreme Heat Risk warning for temperatures of 111–117°F. The heat dome has also dramatically expanded northward, with new Extreme Heat Watches issued for Montana counties expecting 100–110°F and overnight lows in the 70s — providing virtually no relief.

events.title: Europe Heat Dome Escalates — Berlin Hits 37.5°C; 40°C+ Forecast to Persist Into August
events.location: Germany, France, United Kingdom, Spain, and broader Western Europe
events.summary: The European heat dome has intensified and expanded eastward, with Berlin recording 37.5°C on July 30 — among the highest temperatures in the city's modern history for this period — while Paris reached 31°C and London 26.7°C, both still significantly above seasonal norms. Ensemble forecast models cited by severe-weather.eu indicate mid- to upper-air thermal anomalies tracking into the 99th percentile, with temperatures exceeding 40°C forecast to continue across Central and Southern Europe well into August. The World Meteorological Organization has issued warnings about the compounding health, economic, and wildfire risks posed by the ongoing European heat emergency.

events.title: Oregon Wildfire Complex Explodes — Bench Fire at 0% Containment; FEMA Denies Emergency Funding
events.summary: A cluster of fast-moving wildfires is burning across north-central and eastern Oregon, with the Bench Fire near Warm Springs the most critical — having burned 6,963 acres with 0% containment and prompting Level 2 'GET SET' evacuation orders as of July 28–29. The Brewer Fire stands at 10% containment and the Akawa Butte Fire at just 6%, with dry, gusty conditions across the region forecast to worsen through Saturday under multiple active NWS Fire Weather Watches. The situation drew significant political attention after FEMA denied emergency funding requests for the wildfires, prompting Oregon's U.S. senators to formally demand answers from the agency.

events.title: Northeast US Flooding Continues — Active Warnings Across Upstate New York
events.location: Albany, Schenectady, Columbia, Greene, Rensselaer Counties, New York, USA
events.summary: Flood warnings remained active into the morning of July 30 across multiple upstate New York counties including Albany, Schenectady, Rensselaer, Columbia, and Greene, as rivers, creeks, and streams continued running above flood stage following the multi-day flash flood emergency. Numerous roads remain closed due to inundation, with emergency managers warning against driving through flooded roadways, and additional heavy rain potential persisting in parts of New Hampshire overnight. While the acute life-threatening flash flood emergency phase from July 29 has begun to wind down, the lingering riverine flooding across the Capital Region represents a continued severe hazard.

events.title: M5.0 Earthquake Strikes Texas Panhandle — Strongest in the Region in a Century
events.location: Roberts County (38 km SSE of Spearman), Texas Panhandle, USA
events.summary: A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck northwestern Roberts County in the Texas Panhandle on July 23 at 05:21 CDT, registering 498 felt reports across the region and making it the fourth earthquake at or above M5.0 ever recorded in the Texas Panhandle — and the strongest in approximately 100 years. The USGS recorded the shallow event at a depth of 5.7 km, consistent with the shallow induced or tectonic seismicity historically associated with the region's oil and gas production. No structural damage or injuries have been reported, but the unusual magnitude and broad felt extent have drawn scientific attention to ongoing seismic risk in an area not typically associated with significant earthquakes.

events.title: Shanghai Issues Orange High-Temperature Warning as City Hits 39.2°C
events.summary: Shanghai's Meteorological Observatory issued an orange high-temperature warning signal as the city recorded a maximum temperature of 39.2°C on July 30, well above the seasonal average of 32–36°C and driven by the same broad high-pressure system baking much of East Asia. The alert level is the second-highest in China's warning hierarchy, indicating a significant public health risk particularly for outdoor workers, the elderly, and those without air conditioning. The heat is consistent with a broader East Asian heat pattern, with Tokyo also recording 35.1°C and Beijing at 35.5°C, though Shanghai's reading is the most anomalous relative to its typical summer range.

articles.title: Shanghai Meteorological Observatory issued an orange high-temperature warning signal
